title: How to Survive a Plane Crash
lines: Most plane crashes are survivable. | What you do in the next ninety seconds decides if you walk away.
Seventy percent of fatal crashes happen during takeoff, climb-out, approach and landing: | barely six percent of the flight.
So when you sit down, count the rows to your nearest exit. | In smoke, you'll find it by touch.
Keep your seatbelt low and tight, | and keep your shoes on.
If the crew shouts {“brace”,~"brace",} | head down against the seat in front, feet flat on the floor.
When the plane {stops,/~stops,} leave your bag. | Planes are built so everyone can get out in ninety seconds. | Grabbing luggage has cost lives.
Where do you sit when you fly? | Tell me in the comments.
